learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery of craftsmanship and safety through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of craftsmanship and safety.
Check, revise, or improve work about craftsmanship and safety using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about craftsmanship and safety.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.

task_brief: This is day 11 of "Materials, Techniques, and Design". That is unit 2 in grade 5. Today is an unit assessment about craftsmanship and safety. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Design a small collection around a shared theme using at least two media. Today helps by working on craftsmanship and safety. Your unit also covers drawing tools, paint or color media, collage and printmaking, and three-dimensional construction. Today counts for a grade. Do it on your own.
primary_task: Do the unit task for craftsmanship and safety on your own. Make what the task asks for. Show your process, not just the finished piece. Check it against the criteria before you hand it in. Then judge it yourself. What did you want? What did it really do? Where is the gap? Everything must be your own work. You never have to perform in public, use a camera, record your voice, or take a photo to pass. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about craftsmanship and safety. It is part of "Materials, Techniques, and Design". Later days in this unit cover other things, like drawing tools. Before you stop, do this check: Rate confidence in craftsmanship and safety, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting craftsmanship and safety.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for craftsmanship and safety follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for craftsmanship and safety, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for craftsmanship and safety works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of craftsmanship and safety, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking craftsmanship and safety mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply craftsmanship and safety under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on craftsmanship and safety rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
